cards.b: 1905-c.1910. Pure, non-natural colour. Matisse, Derain. 'Wild beasts'.
Art showing inner feeling through distortion and strong colour. Munch, Kirchner.
Objects broken into geometric shapes and shown from several viewpoints. Picasso and Braque.
Analytic (c.1908-12): browns and greys, fragments. Synthetic (from 1912): brighter, simpler, collage.
Picasso, 1937, about the bombing of Guernica in the Spanish Civil War. Museo Reina Sofia, Madrid.
Italian movement (1909): speed, machines, modern life. Boccioni, Balla.
From 1916 in Zurich: anti-war, anti-art, chance and found objects. Duchamp, Hannah Höch.
An ordinary manufactured object presented as art, e.g. Duchamp's Fountain (1917).
From 1924: dreams and the unconscious. Dali, Magritte, Miro.
1940s-50s USA: large gestural abstraction. Pollock (drip), Rothko (colour blocks).
1950s-60s: popular culture and mass media. Warhol, Lichtenstein, Hamilton.
Comic-strip images with Ben-Day dots and bold outlines.
Art in which the idea matters more than the object, e.g. Sol LeWitt's instruction drawings.
2010 installation at Tate Modern of millions of hand-painted porcelain seeds.
